title: Status Epileptikus
subtitle: Kimi rerun: neuro_epilepsy
summary: Kuliah komprehensif tentang status epileptikus (SE) yang mencakup definisi (definisi 5-menit dan 30-menit), klasifikasi (konvulsif vs non-konvulsif, generalisasi vs fokal), epidemiologi, etiologi, patofisiologi (eksitotoksisitas, disfungsi autonomik), gambaran klinis, pendekatan diagnosis (laboratorium, EEG, neuroimaging), protokol manajemen bertahap (benzodiazepin, fenytoin/valproat, SE refrakter dengan agen anestesi), komplikasi, dan prognosis. Menekankan algoritma terapi yang bergantung pada waktu di mana keterlambatan memperburuk outcome.
Operational definition: 5 minutes of continuous seizures OR two or more discrete seizures without full recovery between
Time-dependent treatment: benzodiazepines (0-5 min), IV antiepileptics (5-20 min), anesthetic agents (20-60 min) for refractory SE
Mortality increases with duration: ~3% at 10-29 min, 19% at >30 min, 32% at >60 min
learning_goals: Mendefinisikan status epileptikus menggunakan kriteria berbasis waktu
Mengklasifikasikan SE ke dalam tipe konvulsif dan non-konvulsif
Menerapkan protokol terapi bertahap untuk SE
Menatalaksana status epileptikus refrakter dengan agen anestesi
key_points: Operational definition: 5 minutes of continuous seizures OR two or more discrete seizures without full recovery between
Time-dependent treatment: benzodiazepines (0-5 min), IV antiepileptics (5-20 min), anesthetic agents (20-60 min) for refractory SE
Mortality increases with duration: ~3% at 10-29 min, 19% at >30 min, 32% at >60 min
Non-convulsive SE (NCSE) requires EEG for diagnosis - maintain high index of suspicion in altered mental status after seizure
Refractory SE requires continuous EEG monitoring, anesthetic agents (midazolam, propofol, pentobarbital), and ICU-level care

sections.title: Definisi dan Klasifikasi

content.text: STATUS EPILEPTICUS (SE) is defined as: (1) 5 minutes or more of continuous clinical and/or electrographic seizure activity; OR (2) recurrent seizure activity without recovery (return to baseline) between seizures. Operational time points: T1 (5 minutes) = time when treatment should begin; T2 (30 minutes) = time when risk of neuronal injury increases significantly. CLASSIFICATION: By motor activity: Convulsive SE (CSE) = tonic-clonic movements; Non-convulsive SE (NCSE) = altered mental status without convulsions; Myoclonic SE. By EEG pattern: Generalized SE; Focal SE. By treatment response: Early SE (0-5 min); Established SE (5-20 min, responds to first-line); Refractory SE (RSE) (20-60 min, fails first and second line); Super-refractory SE (>60 min or recurs after anesthetic withdrawal).
Do not wait 30 minutes to treat - begin treatment at 5 minutes per operational definition

sections.title: Etiologi dan Patofisiologi

content.text: ETIOLOGY: Acute symptomatic (stroke, trauma, infection, metabolic derangement, hypoxia, drug withdrawal); Remote symptomatic (epilepsy with breakthrough seizures, missed medications); Progressive symptomatic (brain tumor, neurodegenerative disease). Common triggers: antiepileptic drug non-adherence (most common in known epileptics), alcohol withdrawal, CNS infection, stroke, metabolic (hypoglycemia, hyponatremia, hypocalcemia, uremia, hepatic encephalopathy). PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: Initially, compensatory mechanisms maintain seizure threshold (increased GABA, enhanced receptor sensitivity). After 30 minutes, these fail: GABA receptors internalize (reduced sensitivity to benzodiazepines), NMDA receptors traffic to surface (enhanced excitotoxicity), autonomic dysfunction (hypertension, tachycardia, hyperthermia, sweating, arrhythmias), excitotoxic neuronal damage (glutamate surge, calcium influx, free radical production).
Penyebab: stroke, trauma, infeksi, metabolic, hipoksia, withdraw obat
Pemicu paling umum: non-adherensi OAE, withdraw alkohol
Setelah 30 menit: internalisasi reseptor GABA, eksitotoksisitas
Disfungsi autonomik: hipertensi, takikardi, hipertermi
After 30 minutes, GABA receptor internalization makes benzodiazepines less effective - this is why early treatment is critical

sections.title: Gambaran Klinis dan Diagnosis

content.text: CONVULSIVE SE: Generalized tonic-clonic activity lasting >5 minutes; may become subtle (decreased motor activity) after 30-60 min despite ongoing EEG seizure activity; coma between seizures without recovery; autonomic instability (tachycardia, hypertension, hyperthermia, diaphoresis, pupillary changes); respiratory compromise. NON-CONVULSIVE SE: Altered mental status (confusion, decreased responsiveness, coma) without convulsive activity; may follow CSE (patient fails to wake up after clinical seizures stop); requires EEG for diagnosis. EEG patterns: spike-wave at 3 Hz (typical absence), focal rhythmic activity, periodic discharges. DIAGNOSTIC WORKUP: Blood glucose (immediately), electrolytes (Na, Ca, Mg), renal function, LFTs, ABG, toxicology screen, antiepileptic drug levels, CBC. CT head to rule out structural cause. LP if infection suspected. EEG as soon as possible (especially if NCSE suspected or RSE management).
CSE: aktivitas tonik-klonik >5 menit, disfungsi autonomik
NCSE: altered mental status tanpa konvulsi, butuh EEG
Pemeriksaan: gula darah, elektrolit, CT kepala, EEG
LP jika dicurigai infeksi
Always check blood glucose first in any seizure presentation - hypoglycemia is reversible and treatable

sections.title: Protokol Terapi Bertahap

content.text: PHASE 1 - STABILIZATION (0-5 min): ABCs, vital signs, IV access, blood glucose, labs, position patient to prevent injury, O2 if needed. PHASE 2 - FIRST-LINE (0-10 min): Benzodiazepines (most effective in first 20 min). Options: Lorazepam 0.1 mg/kg IV (max 4 mg), may repeat once; OR Midazolam 0.2 mg/kg IM (if no IV access) or 0.2 mg/kg buccal/IN; OR Diazepam 0.15-0.2 mg/kg IV. PHASE 3 - SECOND-LINE (10-20 min): If seizures continue after benzodiazepines. ONE of: Phenytoin 20 mg/kg IV at max 50 mg/min (monitor BP, ECG); OR Valproate 30-40 mg/kg IV; OR Levetiracetam 60 mg/kg IV (up to 4500 mg); OR Phenobarbital 20 mg/kg IV. PHASE 4 - REFRACTORY SE (20-60 min): If seizures continue after adequate first and second line. Admit to ICU, intubate if needed, continuous EEG. ONE of: Midazolam infusion 0.2 mg/kg bolus then 0.05-2 mg/kg/h; OR Propofol 1-2 mg/kg bolus then 20-100 mcg/kg/min (caution: propofol infusion syndrome >48h); OR Pentobarbital 5-15 mg/kg bolus then 0.5-5 mg/kg/h.
Doses are maximums - always monitor vitals during phenytoin infusion (hypotension, arrhythmia risk)

sections.title: SE Refrakter dan Prognosis

content.text: REFRACTORY SE MANAGEMENT: ICU admission, continuous EEG monitoring (burst suppression or seizure suppression for 24-48h before weaning), supportive care (mechanical ventilation, hemodynamic support, temperature management). Treat underlying cause. Consider alternative diagnoses (pseudoseizures, metabolic coma). COMPLICATIONS: Cardiovascular (arrhythmia, hypotension, cardiac arrest), respiratory (aspiration pneumonia, respiratory failure), neurological (excitotoxic injury, cerebral edema, permanent cognitive deficits), metabolic (rhabdomyolysis, lactic acidosis, hyperthermia, DIC), autonomic storm. PROGNOSIS: Mortality 10-20% for GCSE overall. Factors associated with worse outcome: older age, longer SE duration, acute symptomatic etiology, refractory SE, comorbidities. Good prognostic factors: younger age, idiopathic/cryptogenic etiology, shorter duration, prompt treatment. Mortality by duration: ~3% at 10-29 min, 19% at >30 min, 32% at >60 min.
RSE: ICU, EEG kontinu, ventilasi mekanik jika diperlukan
Komplikasi: aritmia, aspirasi, cedera otak, rabdomiolisis
Mortalitas: 10-20% GCSE; meningkat dengan durasi
Faktor buruk: usia tua, durasi panjang, refrakter
Mortality increases with every minute of untreated SE - aggressive early treatment is the key to improving outcomes
